name: smwmusic-a-ha-take-on-me-invincibility-remix
title: A-ha - Take On Me (Invincibility Remix)
description:
This is to go even further beyond!!!

It's one of A-Ha's best known songs, Take On Me, aka the song that bops every time it's played at a party. It's been remade in a style that's supposed to be used as the music for an invincibility star.

There are two versions of the song:
- Global: This one uses @8 for the bass and @10 for the bass drum. It's optimized to work with the global songs, so you're probably gonna want to use this one if you want it to be your invincibility theme (or p-switch as well). But you can use it as your local song as well.
- Local: This one uses @14 for the bass and @21 for the bass drum. This one won't work with the global songs, but it does use a different set of instruments that some may find to be better than the global version.

This can be used as your invincibility theme, p-switch theme, bonus stage, or even as your victory jingle.

description:
ℌ𝔞𝔭𝔭𝔶 ℌ𝔞𝔩𝔩𝔬𝔴𝔢𝔢𝔫!! 🎃

Made a special re-imagined remix of ActRaiser's Fillmore for Halloween. By far one of the most memorable main themes on the system (more than what you can say for Super Castlevania's Theme of Simon) to the point where people can get fooled into thinking this is a Castlevania theme.

This bad boy can fit ghost houses, castles / towers, temples, final areas, or any other kind of stage with dark and haunting auras.

Important:
There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."
- "Bonus End" is disabled.

There are also 3 customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. C Minor (Remix Pitch, turned on default)
2. B Minor (Hellfire Saga Pitch)
3. A# Minor (Custom Pitch)

name: smwmusic-alcahest-a-world-without-soul-the-demon-underworld-remix
title: Alcahest - A World without Soul ~ The Demon Underworld (Remix)
description:
Did an arrangement of The Demon Underworld from Alcahest. Seriously, for an obscure (but really awesome) Super-Famicom-Only Action RPG by HAL, Jun Ishikawa went hard on this OST. This soundtrack feels like a blend of Ishikawa's style in Kirby Super Star with Nobuo Uematsu's style in the SNES Final Fantasy games. It's easily my favorite Kirby soundtrack given its style and the compositions here.

Originally was planning on doing Panakeian Castle, but I thought I'd give a spotlight to the heavily underrated endgame stage theme 'cuz it's amazing. What's with Squaresoft games having amazing endgame themes anyways?

Important:
♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. C Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. C# Minor (Japanese Goblin Pitch)
3. D Minor (Custom Pitch)

versions.title: Alcahest - A World without Soul ~ The Demon Underworld (Remix)

description:
❝ IT'S HAPPY HOUR! ❞
ㅤ- Anton, Antonblast (2024)



Did an arrangement of the 2nd stage theme The Hammer & The Mace ...in Slowroast Sewer from ANTONBLAST
(ft. Ropes 'n Roper from Battletoads & Double Dragon: The Ultimate Team)
. Wanted to give another shot at an indie platformer theme, especially after falling in love with ANTONBLAST last year, and Slowroast Sewer is easily my favorite stage from the game (with my favorite stage theme as well).

Thought the song sounded very similar to that of BT&DD's Stage 3 theme, so I thought it'd be fun to mash those two up for this mix for double the funk!!!

Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End" & P-Switch are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. A Minor (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ2. A# Minor (Custom Pitch 1)
ㅤ3. G# Minor (Custom Pitch 2)
ㅤ4. F# Minor (Custom Pitch 3)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Original Echo Delay, but sacrifices SMW-Compatibility (OG Echo)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. Decreased Echo Delay & Disables Glass Break (Glass Break DISABLED)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ3. No Echo Delay (NO Echo)

This song is overall a mess, both compositionally and mixing-wise, and while I did try to clean up the mixing at least, it's still a bit all over the place.

Probably best suited for a short, hyper boss.

❝ GO BERSERK!! ❞
ㅤ- Kei, Berserk Boy (2024)

ㅤㅤ

Did an arrangement of Dire Dancing (Dark Fortress Zone 1) from Berserk Boy. Had this one sitting on my PC since 2024, and I wanted to finish it for a while since it's another Mega-Man-inspired indie banger that the whole world needs to know about!!

Important:
ㅤ♠ What's disabled:
ㅤㅤ - "Bonus End" (@7)
ㅤㅤ - "P-Switch" (@12) ← (I did put the Chrono Trigger Bongo in that spot if you just so happen to need it)
ㅤㅤ - Yoshi SFX (@15)
ㅤㅤ - Thunder SFX

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. G Minor (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ2. G# Minor (Custom Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Original Echo Delay, but sacrifices SMW-Compatibility (OG Echo)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. Decreased Echo Delay (LOWER Echo)ㅤ[turned on by default]

This one is hard to port due to the game's sound driver (programmed by OeRSTED) not being supported by vgmtrans. So I used SPCtoMML, and optimized it as soon as I could, even changing the instrument pitch data.

This is the sampled version.

description:

It also brings little variations in the flute and choir lines as well as some octave changes.

Very satisfying, serene vibes, useful for chill levels where flying or clouds are involved.

And that's one more song I was able to cover by ear! Now I find it pretty addictive to listen to.

description:

The duration is shortened a bit as to not insist on the non-melody aspects of the song.

It is probably best fit for overworlds and cutscenes, but can also work in levels that have a timer shorter than the song... Which isn't really a problem either since I gave a loop after a short silence.

It has been showcase at C3 Winter 2022.

This is my first attempt at a non-SNES port, but I guess it doesn't really count because the GBA is somewhat similar to the SNES hardware-wise :P

Anyway, huge thanks to musicalman for his Samples of Insanity pack! That's where I got most of the samples I used here. And thanks to Pinci too, for helping me find a water SFX sample!

Warning: Incompatible with Blarggs and the Thunder SFX! Also, please don't use this for level 0/100, because the Bonus End jingle won't play correctly. I figured these two samples were fine to exclude since the song doesn't quite fit a lava (Blargg), dramatic/final (Thunder) or bonus level.

❝ 𝔑𝔬𝔱𝔥𝔦𝔫𝔤 𝔶𝔬𝔲 𝔰𝔞𝔶 𝔴𝔦𝔩𝔩 𝔰𝔱𝔬𝔭 𝔪𝔢! 𝔓𝔯𝔢𝔭𝔞𝔯𝔢 𝔱𝔬 𝔡𝔦𝔢! ❞
ㅤ- Julius Belmont, Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow (2003)



Did a second arrangement of Don't Wait Until Night from Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow (originally from Haunted Castle). Celebrating 6 years of SNES-mix uploads (5 years on YouTube specifically) with arranging the song that would be my first ever mix uploaded onto YouTube. I thought it'd be fun to go back and do another "re-remix" of an old mix of mine, though this time, I'd base it off both the Haunted Castle & Aria of Sorrow versions rather than basing it off just Haunted Castle's version.

I have plans to do more "re-remixes" of some very old tracks in the future, and this is one of my first ones I'll be doing.

Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, Yoshi SFX, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. D Minor (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ2. E Minor (Remix I Pitch)
ㅤ3. C Minor (NES Pitch)
ㅤ4. D# Minor (Whip Rush!! Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Original Echo Delay, but sacrifices SMW-Compatibility (OG Echo)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. Decreased Echo Delay, but disables outro (DISABLES Outro)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ3. Drastically Decreased Echo Delay (LOWER Echo)

versions.title: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow - Whip, Cross, & Justice!! ✝️ ~ Don't Wait Until Night x Heart of Fire (Remix II)

title: Castlevania II: Simon's Quest - Dracula's Bloodfest ~ Bloody Tears (Remix)
description:
𝕾𝖙𝖎𝖑𝖑 𝖚𝖙𝖙𝖊𝖗𝖎𝖓𝖌 𝖙𝖍𝖊 𝖘𝖆𝖒𝖊 𝖓𝖔𝖓𝖘𝖊𝖓𝖘𝖊. 𝕹𝖔 𝖒𝖆𝖙𝖙𝖊𝖗. 𝕹𝖔𝖜 𝖎𝖘 𝖙𝖍𝖊 𝖙𝖎𝖒𝖊 𝖙𝖔 𝖕𝖚𝖙 𝖆𝖘𝖎𝖉𝖊 𝖞𝖔𝖚𝖗 𝖜𝖊𝖆𝖐 𝖍𝖚𝖒𝖆𝖓 𝖘𝖎𝖉𝖊, 𝖆𝖓𝖉 𝖏𝖔𝖎𝖓 𝖒𝖊 𝖎𝖓 𝖗𝖊𝖒𝖆𝖐𝖎𝖓𝖌 𝖙𝖍𝖎𝖘 𝖜𝖔𝖗𝖑𝖉!


Bloody Tears from Worst Metroidvania ever Castlevania II: Simon's Quest. Since everyone seems to like porting the Super Castlevania IV version more than the original, I had to do my part and give you guys my rendition of the original song. Nothing way too extreme, but nothing simple either.

This song could fit intense castle levels, fast-paced levels, dark levels, and maybe even some bosses

Note: There's a !!! READ ME !!!.txt file which has the sample bank for the song. You need to copy that over to Addmusic_sample groups.txt or else the song will not work. Also you go into the song file, you can adjust the pitch to five different options that are on there: a# minor (Default), b minor (Hyper-Realistic by Lui37), a minor (Custom one but I call it "Mega Man"), g minor (I think it's custom, but I call it anyways "Touhou" because it's always about Touhou!), and f minor (Super Castlevania IV).

Also shoutouts to @springhakurei "Jeto" on twitter. Jeto makes some awesome / kawaii art on Small Richter, Touhou girls, and a lotta Simon... and I mean a lot.

title: Castlevania - Rise of the Vampire Killer ~ Vampire Killer (Remix)
description:
𝕯𝖎𝖊, 𝖒𝖔𝖓𝖘𝖙𝖊𝖗! 𝖄𝖔𝖚 𝖉𝖔𝖓'𝖙 𝖇𝖊𝖑𝖔𝖓𝖌 𝖎𝖓 𝖙𝖍𝖎𝖘 𝖜𝖔𝖗𝖑𝖉!

The first stage of Castlevania 1 that became one of the three definitive theme songs of the Castlevania franchise. A bit more intensive than the original version, but that's how I like it. It also has an ending similar to that the of Castlevania: Rondo of Blood version of this song... or is it...

This song could fit dark stages, castles, intense ghost houses, and maybe even factories if you're crazy enough to use them in those levels.

Note: There's a READ ME!!.txt file with the sample group necessary for this song to work. All you need to do is copy what's inside and place it into the Addmusic_sample groups.txt file or else an error will come up when you try to export this into your romhack. The Thunder SFX is not compatible with this song.

name: smwmusic-castlevania-symphony-of-the-night-blood-relations
title: Castlevania: Symphony of the Night - Blood Relations
description:
This is the theme that plays when you're fighting Richter Belmont, the game's fake final boss, in Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. This is a very final-like song, but it's also a very weird and "janky" one, thanks to the 5/8 time signature this song is mostly in, which, along with the overall strong presence of dissonance, gives off a very great sense of unsettlement and tragedy to the battle itself, to differentiate from other final boss themes.

But yeah, like I said here, honestly, in my opinion, I think the best way this could fit is really only for final boss battles. You could probably find a better use for this port outside of that purpose tho, maybe I'm just being dumb. :V

versions.title: Castlevania: Symphony of the Night - Blood Relations

description:
Demon, death is too good for you! 🦇

Did an arrangement of Dracula's Castle from Castlevania: Symphony of the Night to celebrate the Return to Castlevania DLC for Dead Cells.

We all know how iconic it is! It's the first thing you hear once you enter Dracula's doors into his newest and most biggest castle (at the time). It's such an amazing theme song for the amazing game that changed the world forever!!!

Hooded's Obsessive Shilling Over Dead Cells & Why You Should Play It
Dead Cells is a must-play for any Castlevania, Metroidvania, and Rogue-lite fans. It's an underrated masterpiece that continues to be a better live-service than every live-service game out there (w/o even being a real live-service game in the first-place) w/ constant updates adding new content to the already-finished game. Its combat is fluent, its level design is perfect, its atmosphere is tense and Castlevania-like, IT'S ALL PERFECT, AND YOU SHOULD PLAY IT!!!

SERIOUSLY! WHAT ARE YOU DOING WITH YOUR LIFE RIGHT NOW?!?! GO BUY IT!!! PLZ!!! IT'S SO FREAKING AMAZING!!!

🦇 ℌ𝔞𝔭𝔭𝔶 ℌ𝔞𝔩𝔩𝔬𝔴𝔢𝔢𝔫!! 🎃

Did a more funky arrangement of Wandering Ghosts from Castlevania: Symphony of the Night for my Halloween Special (coming up on... Halloween). It's been a while since I last did my previous Castlevania remix, and I thought I'd do one from one of the coolest games to exist. Wandering Ghosts is my favorite song in the game. It's so freaking good, and I can't believe they'd put this banger in a Colosseum that you barely spend much time in.

description:
Ported by request. 7 custom samples (6.4KiB).

It was a pain to figure out the notes for the cabasa, but I think it turned out mostly okay.

The lower harpsichord notes are on Ch6 out of necessity (as far as wanting to have a dedicated channel for the flute delay/echo, anyway). It's not particularly loud so I imagine that if it gets cut off by sound effects, it won't be missed.

Could work well in a puzzle-type cave atmosphere (not familiar with the series so I may be way off as to how it should fit in).

description:
Did an arrangement of the Main BGM from China Warrior (aka The Kung Fu in Japan) for the TurboGrafx-16 / PC-Engine. Yeah, a game where you play as knock-off Bruce Lee and beat up some nuns has a banger OST (even though it's like 3 full songs and a couple jingles). Ended up playing this on my TurboGrafx-16 Mini back in December and fell in love with this theme.

I actually did start this port way back in April before getting too caught up on other songs. Luckily, I was able to get it finished now, and thank god I did. This song deserves some love, even if you don't ever plan on ever playing the game.

This is pretty lengthy song and also a great fit for auto-scrollers.

Important:
There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. C Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. C# Minor (Custom Pitch 1)
3. B Minor (Custom Pitch 2)

ㅤ0. No Death SFX [turned on by default]
ㅤ1. Death SFX


Mod Note: If using this as a global song (such as the death or game over songs), you will need to add ! to the line featuring @14 in Addmusic_sample_groups.txt for it to sound as intended.

Update:
Added an option to change the sample in the song (for those who want to use it globally w/o any workarounds):
ㅤ1. @1 (Works globally by default) [turned on by default]
ㅤ2. @14

description:
Did a birthday special arrangement of Corridors Of Time from Chrono Trigger. Thought it'd be great to celebrate my birthday with another special remix once again and also give myself an excuse to make a remix of a Chrono Trigger theme but make it SPECIAL.

Chrono Trigger is one of my favorite games of all-time, and I believe the game deserves as much praise as it keeps on getting. It's not only a one-of-a-kind SquEnix RPG, but also probably one of the best video games ever made. It's easily one of the best experiences I ever had with a video game, and I'm sure it was the same for morbillions of others as well.

Important:
♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.

description:
❝ 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐩𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐀𝐫𝐞 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐌𝐞𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐅𝐨𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐓𝐚𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐎𝐟 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐬. 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲’𝐫𝐞 𝐌𝐞𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐅𝐨𝐫 𝐒𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦. ❞
ㅤ- Melchior, 1995

Did an arrangement of Battle 1 from Chrono Trigger in memory of Akira Toriyama. Not often I do something like this, but as fan of Chrono Trigger and huge fan of Akira Toriyama's work & art, I thought it'd be great to dedicate this one to him.

Chrono Trigger's Battle theme is one of my favorite battle themes in any RPG

Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," Yoshi SFX, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. D Minor (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ2. C Minor (Custom Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Default Echo Delay, but sacrifices the P-Switch Jingle & @9 is replaced with @0 (Default Echo Delay)
ㅤ2. Decreases Echo Delay (Lower Echo Delay)ㅤ[turned on by default]

It's worth noting that the SNES version of the game had an entirely original soundtrack composed in-house at Koei, so this tune is not present in other versions of the game. The original composer is unknown.

This song could work well in an epic/dramatic cutscene, as well as (obviously) the title screen of your hack. Due to the climactic and triumphant nature of the track, it may also work near the game's ending. A few people on Discord said that it would be fit for use in a kaizo hack, as well.

name: smwmusic-contra-nes-rambo-gone-commando-jungle-stage-remix
title: Contra (NES) - Rambo Gone Commando ~ Jungle Stage (Remix)
description:
⬆️ ⬆️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬅️ ➡️ ⬅️ ➡️ 🅱️ 🅰️ START

Arranged the Jungle Stage theme (NES Version) from Contra. A song I kept forgetting to do until now (thank god!), and it's another classic and memorable 80s banger from a classic game. Absolutely love this song and this game.

Important:
♠ "Bonus End" is disabled.

There are also 2 customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. F / C Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. F# / C# Minor (Custom Pitch)

title: Cosmic Psycho (X68000) - Neptune

A song from some obscure game that I know nothing about for an archaic computer.

A lovely swing composition that translates super well into SMW instruments. Special thanks to Ethelfleda for posting this song in the Discord which led to me discovering it, and to sincx for helping me extract the note data from the original game.

Originally ported for Superfamicompo 3.

description:
A very shooter game-sounding song from Cosmic Psycho. It's fairly short, and is very upbeat.

Includes a define that I completely forgot about until now, which lets you switch the lead in the climax of the song between a hybrid @1/@2, and @17.

title: Cosmo Gang: The Video - Stage Theme 2 (Segment 2)

Note that the percussion has some clicking because of the trick I used to remove the staccato on the percussion channel.

name: smwmusic-cosmoclock-contraption
title: Cosmoclock Contraption
description:
A groovy tune originally composed for Superfamicompo 5's challenge category.

It makes me think of some kind of countdown, and an ensuing launch into the vastness of space. Maybe it's because the triplet-y section reminds me of Gradius music lol.

(Uses optimized SMW Thunder instead of default like the original submission because of ARAM limitations.
Not compatible with Yoshi or Bonus End for that reason.)

name: smwmusic-cotton-fluff-clouds
title: Cotton Fluff Clouds
description:
A fast-paced cheery song that could fit clouds or grasslands.

Note that it only uses two custom samples, and uses mostly vanilla instruments. With some effort, it could probably be unsampled and sound almost the same.

0 - Default in-game version
1 - Extended OST version (3:04, 0x0EB7)
2 - In-game version but with the addition of the drum intro from CTR Nitro-Fueled (0x0D89)

title: Crash Nitro Kart - Electron Avenue / Magnetic Mayhem
description:
An upbeat techno theme that plays in Electron Avenue, the fan favorite track from Crash Nitro Kart which is set in a futuristic city at night. In CTR Nitro-Fueled, this track was massively revamped with a neon vaporwave-like aesthetic.

Also for some reason this song plays in Magnetic Mayhem, a battle arena based on Assembly Lane, which doesn't really fit.

You can define in the .txt file which variation you want to use:
0 - Default in-game version
1 - Extended OST version (3:14, 0x0AC0)

Note: The OST version of this song is incompatible with thunder, blargg and Yoshi sound effects and the vanilla bonus end jingle.

title: Crash Nitro Kart - Fenomena Hubworld
description: A slow-paced and calm theme that plays in the third hub of Crash Nitro Kart, the planet Fenomena which is a deserted planet with many clockwork buildings. This theme remixes the main motif of Clockwork Wumpa, one of the tracks from this hub.

name: smwmusic-crash-nitro-kart-hyper-spaceway-victorious-velo
title: Crash Nitro Kart - Hyper Spaceway + Victorious Velo
description:
An intense final boss theme that plays in Hyper Spaceway, the last track from Crash Nitro Kart and the track where the race against the game's final boss, Emperor Velo XXVII takes place. This track also has an alternate version from the game's OST called Victorious Velo, which is an acoustic and more calm remix.

You can define in the .txt file which variation you want to use:
0 - Default in-game version
1 - In-game version but with the addition of the drum intro from CTR Nitro-Fueled (0x0AD5)
2 - OST remixed version called Victorious Velo (3:15, 0x08C5, tags: calm and jungle)

versions.title: Crash Nitro Kart - Hyper Spaceway + Victorious Velo

name: smwmusic-crash-nitro-kart-inferno-island-terra-drome

A fast paced tropical theme that remixes the ending motif of Crash Cove from CTR and plays in Inferno Island, the first track from Crash Nitro Kart, which is very similar to Crash Cove in a lot of ways, especially in its original version. It also plays in Terra Drome, an unlockable temple themed battle arena.

You can define in the .txt file which variation you want to use:
0 - Default in-game version
1 - Extended OST version (3:14, 0x1157)

Note: by default, both versions are NOT compatible with thunder/blargg, Yoshi and Bonus End, but you can set in the txt to disable the echo and make it compatible

name: smwmusic-crash-nitro-kart-main-theme
title: Crash Nitro Kart - Main Theme
description:
The upbeat and triumphant main theme of Crash Nitro Kart.

This includes three variations of this track, which can be defined in the .txt file:

0 - Normal version, plays on the main menu
1 - XBox version of the menu theme, which is slightly longer by featuring an extended bassline (0:39, 0x03DE)
2 - Opening version, has an intro and an extension, this port is slightly different than the original version as that version features an abridged version of the main motif that gets mixed with the intro voices, and this version keeps it on the same length as the menu versions (1:04, 0x04EC)

name: smwmusic-crash-nitro-kart-meteor-gorge-frozen-frenzy
title: Crash Nitro Kart - Meteor Gorge / Frozen Frenzy
description:
An upbeat and funky theme that plays in Meteor Gorge, a track that mixes ice and lava in an industrial setting. It also plays in Frozen Frenzy, a battle arena inspired by that track.

You can define in the .txt file which variation you want to use:
0 - Default in-game version
1 - In-game version but with the addition of the drum intro from CTR Nitro-Fueled (0x0EB2)
2 - Extended OST version (2:46, 0x1071)
3 - Extended OST version but replaces the pizzicato sample with the guitar from the default version

Note: the normal OST version is incompatible with thunder, blargg and Yoshi sound effects and the vanilla bonus end jingle. This is not the case for the alternate variation which replaces the pizzicato with the guitar.

versions.title: Crash Nitro Kart - Meteor Gorge / Frozen Frenzy

name: smwmusic-crystalized-fractal-realm
title: Crystalized Fractal Realm
description:
Some of you wondered whether or not the Crystal Castle was the ghost house theme... well, no. This is actually the one I intended as the ghost house theme. And this is when you get lost in this hall of mirrors... lots of reflections, but which is the real one?

NOTE: Given how long the song is in the first place (longer than 999 seconds to SMW's standard), a ghost house with no timer would probably work best for this particular song... or use a 16-bit timer patch.

NOTE: The Hurry Up! effect may not appear to speed up all sections of the song, mostly due to lag-related effects from me using a high tempo to minimize staccato (in addition to using light staccato in the first place) as well as usually using volume fades across all of the channels in at least one case. The nature of the song tends to mitigate the usual lag-related gotchas, though, as usually the lag is occurring in the sections where the volume fades are occurring on all of the channels in one go, subsequently meaning that the lag ends when the fades stop occurring on all of the channels at once, which is neatly timed to the end of a section as well.

name: smwmusic-deltarune-faint-courage
title: Deltarune - Faint Courage
description:
This is not
your fate...!

Please,
don't give up!

Come on,
that all you got!?

Kris,
get up...!

----------

This is the Game Over theme for Deltarune chapters 2 and onward!

For once, I have actually completed one of my 7 bazillion WIPs.

I don't really see this working practically as anything more than a game-over theme, and I wouldn't advise against using it as anything else either as channels #6 and #7 do have noticeable audio in them. I might fix it at a later time but for now I'm more or less satisfied with this.

I tried to go for a chiptune-ish sounding beginning like Deltarune has then transitioning it to use more instruments and panning in the second half.

I hope to do more Deltarune and Undertale music in the future! Though theres a lot of unique sounds and instruments that I'm having trouble replicating with default samples.

----------

THEN THE WORLD
WAS COVERED
IN DARKNESS.

title: Donkey Kong Country 2: Diddy's Kong Quest - Mercy is for Monkeys! 🏴‍☠️ ~ Crocodile Cacophony (Remix)
description:
❝ 𝐍𝐨𝐰 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐈 𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐩𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫, 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐢𝐬 𝐦𝐲 𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐫

ㅤ- King K. Rool, Donkey Kong Country Cartoon (1998)



Did an arrangement of Crocodile Cacophony from the GREATEST GAME EVER MADE!! Did his first theme song last year, so I HAVE TO do his true theme song!!! Took heavy inspiration from both the original and Smash renditions.

Important:
ㅤ♠ What's disabled:
ㅤㅤ - "Bonus End" (@7)
ㅤㅤ - Thunder SFX

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. G Major (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ2. A Major (Croc Isle Pitch)
ㅤ3. G# Major (Finest Hour Pitch)
ㅤ4. F Major (Custom Pitch 1)
ㅤ5. F# Major (Custom Pitch 2)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Original Volume Level (OG Volume)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. Decreased Volume Level (LOWER Volume)ㅤ[turned on by default]

title: Donkey Kong Country x Touhou Koumakyou ~ the Embodiment of the Scarlet Devil - Roses 'N Kruelty 🌹 ~ Gang-Plank Galleon x U.N. Owen was Her? (Remix)
description:
❝ Right, I've had enough of this. It's time for me to get going. So you Kongs better get off of my ship or else! ❞
ㅤ- King K. Rool, Donkey Kong Country [GBA] (2003)


Did a mashup arrangement of King KAROOL's theme song Gang-Plank Galleon x Flandre Skarlet's theme song U.N. Owen Was Her? from Donkey Kong Country & Touhou 6 Koumakyou ~ the Embodiment of the Skarlet Devil, respektively. Two krazies, two bangers, one psykhotic mix!! This was a mix I planned for at the beginning of the year and, of kourse, expekted it to be one of my more ambitious ones.

Given this mashup's entire premise, I primarily wanted to primarily base this remix off the Smash Ultimate version of K. Rool's theme (given the pace of that version matches up with Flan's theme) while also retaining elements of the original.

Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, Yoshi SFX, & Thunder SFX are disabled.
ㅤ♠ Death sound is gonna sound weird (@0 replaces @9 to save on space).

There are also kustomizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. D Minor (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ2. C Minor (Pseudo Paradise Pitch)
ㅤ3. E Minor (Gouyoku Ibun Pitch)

There are also kustomizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Original Echo Delay, but sacrifices SMW-Compatibility (OG Echo)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. Dekreased Echo Delay, but removes the intro (DISABLES Intro)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ2. DRASTICALLY Dekreased Echo Delay (LOWER Echo)

title: Donkey Kong Land - K. Rool's Rave Party ~ Bad Boss Boogie (Remix)
description:
Did an arrangement of Bad Boss Boogie theme from Donkey Kong Country Land. I can probably say I prefer this soundtrack over Donkey Kong Country 1's OST by a landslide, and this song is one of the reasons why. I mean, it's so simple yet so freaking catchy and was made to be dance music!!!

And my god, it feels so amazing to have finally done a song from my favorite franchise ever. I've been pretty off about doing remixes from the games though in the past 'cuz I always thought my style wouldn't be able to work well for David Wise's / Everlyn Fischer's music given their style is... something else completely! That is until now with this port of the DKL Boss theme. Definitely am doing more songs from this series (especially from DKC2... god bless that game).

Important:
♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

description:
Did an arrangement of the Flooded Ruins stage theme from Donkey Kong Land, Kremlantis. Another one of my favorites from this game and another one that I ended up experimenting with. I've been wanting to do this for some time but kept on forgetting about it.

Once again gonna simp for David Wise here 'cuz goddamn. It doesn't matter what hardware he's working with, if it can produce music, he'll put out some of the best bangers to ever make it on the hardware, and this is another fantastic example of this.

title: Dragon Ball Z: Budokai - The Saiyan, Who controls the Blowing Wind ~ Challengers (Kochiya-Mix)
description:
❝ Hey, it's me Goku! Is that all you got, Frieza? ❞
ㅤ- Sean Schemmel (as Son Goku (aka Kakarot)), 2009



Did an arrangement of Challengers from Dragon Ball Z: Budokai. Just got into Dragon Ball recently and binged through the entirety of OG Dragon Ball, DBZ Kai, and DB Super, and I thought it'd be fun to make a mix of one of the series best themes, and there's no better song to choose than the one I've been listening to way WAY before I got into this series!!

Hooded Edge rambling on about this theme
I LOVE THIS THEME!! Challengers is easily one of my favorite fighting game themes of all-time, and, other than Makafushigi Adventure, this is one other song I primarily think of when it comes to Dragon Ball music. I thought it'd work incredibly well with Sanae's theme from Touhou 10: Mountain of Faith, Faith is for the Transient (I swear, her theme song goes well with nothing but absolute bangers like MM2 Wily's Castle & this song).

I actually remember first hearing this song in a Sonic 1 romhack, Mobius Evolution, and that was years ago, and it was even used as a Super theme in that game too.


Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.

name: smwmusic-ducktales-journey-to-the-very-end-the-moon-remix
title: DuckTales - Journey To The Very End ~ The Moon (Remix)
description:
*A S C E N D S*


Did an arrangement of The Moon stage theme from DuckTales. What can I even say about this track that hasn't been said before. It's easily Disney's most iconic theme they had in any video game of theirs renditions of musicial numbers from the movies don't count. It's been arranged so much to the point where goddamn Jake Kaufman had to cough up a banger arrangement for the remake. It's one of my favorite songs on the NES, especially from a game I generally enjoyed when I was younger.

Important:
♠ "Bonus End" is disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. F# Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. F Minor (Custom Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. Enables Voice Clip, but at the cost of the P-Switch & Thunder SFX
2. Disables Voice Clip (turned on default)

versions.title: DuckTales - Journey To The Very End ~ The Moon (Remix)

𝗡𝗼𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗮𝗹𝘀 𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗰𝗸𝘀... 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝘀!

If you like the song, please check out the original. This 3 minute snippet hardly does it justice.


Come inside, the show's about to start, guaranteed to blow your head apart!

name: smwmusic-endless-determination
title: Endless Determination
description:
My first remix of my own composition (or I guess technically you can call this it's own composition, in which case, this is the fifth finished one).

After re-listening to Endless Nights I wondered if I can make it more boss battle themed and the result was this!

Some parts were from compositions that didn't go anywhere, like the intro, so I reused them, since they fit well here.

Was made to be used in boss battles, but I could also see its use in chase levels or intense castles with lasers.

An alternate version is included, which loops before the original's actual end and prevents it from stopping for a few seconds.

[included are two versions - the only difference between them is boosted volume for the quieter sections]

description:
(My second ever try at porting an existing song.)
This is 'Gymnopédie No. 1', a famous piano piece by Erik Satie. I tried my best to make this sound as piano-like and close to the original as possible without using samples - it might still be lacking a bit, but it's nice enough to listen to at least.
Would work well for extraordinarily calm places, especially cutscenes.

name: smwmusic-escape

description: And as an extra, here is the first ever original compo I did, which as you can tell is obviously built with an timed escape sequence in mind (which is also why the song doesn't loop from the start btw, and why I won't put in a loop since it would lose much of the impact I wanted to portray otherwise). Since this is only usable in a very specific context I dunno how many would bother using this, but it's definitely something to consider if you're planning to have a escape sequence in your own hack either way :P

name: smwmusic-f-zero-silence
title: F-Zero - Silence
description:
My goal for 2019 is to upload more music and generally be more active... and possibly have a shot at mosts!

This is Silence, a moody piece from the original F-Zero that debuted on the SNES in 1990, 1991, and 1992 in Japan, America, and Europe respectively. It's probably one of my favorite games... Great soundtrack, and you get to slam into walls at over 3 times the interstate speed limit and uh, die... While listening to some really catchy music! Even the music that plays after you die is great

Unlike the song's name implies, there is no actual silence. It starts out rather calm, but then the second part of it drops into something less calm that would definitely fit an exciting level.

Accuracy was not in mind when I made this song!

title: Fatal Fury Special - The Last Supper for Geese 🍽️ ~ Soy Sauce for Geese (Remix)
description:
❝ Die like your father, you pin-headed son of an ice cream maker! ❞
ㅤ- Geese Howard, Fatal Fury Special (1993)



Did an arrangement of the one and only, Soy Sauce for Geese from the Fatal Fury franchise. I've been getting into Fatal Fury / King of Fighters recently (they're really great games), and I thought I'd dedicate an arrangement to the one and only Howard Geese's theme 'cuz it is exactly what people say it is: A BANGER!!!

This song has always been fascinating to me because of its fusion of hard rock and honkyoku music that's made the song iconic and also fitting for Geese's character (as gaming's first American Weeb).

Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, Yoshi SFX, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. C Minor w/ Slight Detune (Remix Pitch)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. C Minor (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ3. A Minor (Custom Pitch 1)
ㅤ4. C# Minor (Custom Pitch 2)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Enables the voice clip, but sacrifices SMW-Compatibility (Voice Enabled)ㅤ[Listening-Only]

description:
𝓢𝓽𝓪𝓻𝓴𝓵𝓮, 𝓼𝓽𝓪𝓻𝓴𝓵𝓮 𝓵𝓲𝓽𝓽𝓵𝓮 𝓽𝔀𝓲𝓷𝓴... 𝓝𝓸𝔀 𝓲𝓽'𝓼 𝓽𝓲𝓶𝓮 𝓽𝓱𝓪𝓽 𝔂𝓸𝓾 𝓰𝓾𝔂𝓼 𝓢𝓘𝓝𝓚!!
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ- Gilgamesh, 1992

Did a special arrangement of Battle on the Big Bridge from for my 6K SUBSCRIBER MILESTONE!!!

Gotta be one of the GREATEST RPG boss themes to end all RPG boss themes. Seriously, I love this song SO GODDAMN MUCH!!! Gilgamesh's theme might as well be the Ken Master's Theme of RPGs. It's not only my favorite song in Final Fantasy 5, but also my favorite song in the entire franchise. Shoutout to FINAL FANTASY Record Keeper] for having the best version of the song period (and also being a great reference to use for this port).

Super Castlevania IV fake-ass Trumpet jumpscare. lmao


Important:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," Yoshi, & Thunder SFX are disabled.
‎‎
There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. F Minor (Original Pitch) [turned on by default]

Mod note: reduced the echo delay from $04 to $03 to allow compatibility with the death sound.

description:
❝ 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐞... 𝐃𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐬... 𝐇𝐨𝐩𝐞... 𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐝𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐟𝐫𝐨𝐦? 𝐀𝐧𝐝 𝐰𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐝𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐠𝐨...? 𝐒𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐦𝐞𝐚𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬... 𝐈'𝐥𝐥 𝐝𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐨𝐲 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐦 𝐚𝐥𝐥! ❞
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ- Kefka Palazzo, 1994

Did a special arrangement of Dancing Mad (Part 5) from Final Fantasy VI. A special request from Daizo Dee Von for his hack ~OMH~. Easily one of my favorite final battle themes in the series and also one of the hardest tracks I had to work on. Either way, it was a ton of fun to do!!

credit to Tamaki and their port for the Kefka laughing sound.

Important:

name: smwmusic-final-fantasy-vi-determined-conflict-the-decisive-battle-remix
title: Final Fantasy VI - Determined Conflict ~ The Decisive Battle (Remix)
description:
Did an arrangement of The Decisive Battle from Final Fantasy VI, aka one of the most popular songs in the entirety of RPGs. Easily my favorite track from this fantastic OST / Game and my favorite decisive battle theme in the series bars none. This was definitely in my to-dos for Final Fantasy arrangements, and I went all out on this one like every other song I do. I love this soundtrack so much, and I hope more people get to listen to it (and play the game too)!!

Important:
♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. A Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. A# Minor (Custom Pitch)

name: smwmusic-final-fantasy-vii-mako-reactor
title: Final Fantasy VII - Mako Reactor
description:
The deeply menacing theme representing the Mako Factory from Final Fantasy VII, or as I like to call it "Magitek Research Facility's Younger Brother". Not accurate to the original due to not having the proper samples, so I used some of my own ones. Since I really like the Remake version, I included a small nod to it that plays every second loop if you enable it using the define "LOOP2" (see txt for details). If it's disabled, the size will decrease to 0x042D and the real length will be 1:35.

Includes the option to enable/disable staccato with the staccato define. With it enabled, the size will decrease to 0x05C6 (which really isn't much). If this is enabled along with LOOP2 disabled, it will become 0x0467.

This submission accounts for the max size and length using the various defines.

Song not compatible with P-switch, Bonus End, Thunder, Yoshi, or Blarggs.

Edit: Wrong notes been corrected (to the best of my abilities), tho I kept in the "wrong intro notes" as an option in the "ACCURATE" define because I unironically liked it better. Nameless is the one to thank for pointing where I made mistakes. With ACCURATE disabled (setting it to 1), it'll add 3 extra bytes.

description:

The iconic theme heard when your grandfather clock dials it's chimes. It's also used in the hit indie game "Chipper & Sons Lumber Co." by Scott Cawthon, amongst a few others-less popular-titles.

There are two versions: one specifically used in ~omh~, and one that's compatible with global (lacks any echo, and uses more channels to recreate it). You CAN use the ~omh~ one with echo as a victory theme if you just use it as a local song and set the death theme to the song number in asm/SNES/tweaks.asm.

The ~omh~ version is 0x0097, while the global version is 0x00E0.

If the goal define is 0, the size decreases to 0x005A for ~omh~, while it'll decrease to 0x009D for global.

name: smwmusic-fortress-of-artificial-fabrication
title: Fortress of Artificial Fabrication
description:
Time to infiltrate this place. What are they making here?

This song, which I originally revealed in Super Famicompo 2, actually has a pretty long history. It was originally created on 7/11/12 for something that I never submitted. The biggest thing about it is that it wasn't actual SNES music, but generally speaking it used soundfonts from various games. I revived it after doing some volume balancing, intending on submitting it for the first Super Famicompo, but picked the wrong song by mistake (which was something I prototyped for the same thing). Thus, this instead came out for the second Super Famicompo, which in turn caused me to get contacted about this song being ported shortly after the compo concluded.

I have redone the port myself, mostly to take advantage of more modern techniques that were previously not possible on earlier AddmusicK versions. Plus, the overall filesize is smaller as a result of doing this... well, at least the song data is smaller.

WARNING: This song has multiple stock sample substitutions due to memory constraints, and has a set of sample groups that should be added to the Addmusic_sample groups.txt file to facilitate this. These affect the following:
  • Miss song (uses a non-stock sample)
  • P-Switch song
  • All Thunder-based SFX (including Blargg and affecting $1DF9 SFX IDs $21, $25, $27, $29 and $1DFC SFX IDs $1A, $2C) ($1DFC SFX ID $1A (the Castle Destruction Bomb SFX) is not recommended, mostly because it's quite a bit more reliant on the original sample than the others, being a single note)
  • Yoshi SFX ($1DFC SFX ID $1F) and Bonus End song (uses a non-stock sample)

name: smwmusic-fury-of-the-storm-go-into-the-nightmare
title: Fury of the Storm - Go Into The Nightmare
description:
Lyrics:
Go Into The Nightmare!
Go Into The (Go Into The)
Go Into The Nightmare!
... Let's Go!
Go Into The Nightmare!
Go Into The, Go Into The,
Go Into The Nightmare!
... Let's Go!

(Vocalist is me, Daizo)

The incredibly rocked out boss theme used in the 4th Place WLDC2022 Entry "Fury of the Storm" where you fight Sir Kris Flurry (thank you ChaseNScooter for naming her and yes, she's a her.) As you might be able to tell, it's a song with vocal samples.

"CORRECTNESS" define will change the timing the sample "Let's Go!" is played. 0 is accurate to the contest entry, any other number plays it at it's proper timing.

Song is not compatible with Yoshi, P-switches, Bonus End, Contact/Clap, Thunder, and Blarggs, and Death. Would recommend Retry patch to get around the lack of a death theme. Contact/Clap is at least replaced with the snare included with the song so it still 'sounds' impactful instead of glitched.

PLEASE credit me. I don't sing too often, and I also composed the song itself so I'd very much appreciate the recognition.

title: Ghouls 'n Ghosts (Amiga) - Title Screen
description:
Acoustic guitar-heavy title screen music from the Amiga version of Ghouls 'n Ghosts.

The custom loop version is made in order for the song to loop smoothly, being intended for levels, and it's slightly smaller than the full version (0x0739 bytes). The full version is more for cutscenes and whatnot.

In the full version's text files, there is a #define LOOPABLE. It's set to 1 by default, and when it's set to 0, it will not loop back to the beginning at all, it'll just be still when the song comes to an end.

Incompatible with @7 (bonus end fanfare) and thunder sound effect.
The full version will omit one of the samples under the following defines:
-#define P_SWITCH 1 will enable P-Switch sample and omit Yoshi sample.
-#define P_SWITCH 0 (or other number) will be vice versa.

UPDATE: Corrected a few notes, as well as updating the overdriven guitar sample.

name: smwmusic-goanimate-dance
title: GoAnimate - Dance
description:
Jokes aside, GoAnimate (now known as Vyond) is you guessed it! A website that allows you to animate using drag and drop, even having themes that allow you to create custom characters (e.g. Comedy Worlds, Lil' Peepz, Chibi Peepz, etc.).

It was intended to be an easier and quicker alternative to tools such as Flash, and although initially obscure, it suddenly became popular in the mid-2010s, and nope, it's not because of its easy to use nature, it's not because of one theme (Comedy World) being themed after Family Guy, no no no, it's because of, as mentioned in the picture above, those infamous "you are grounded grounded grounded" videos, often featuring characters from preschool shows such as Caillou, Barney the Dinosaur, Dora the Explorer, Elmo, being you know... grounded, often for literal eternity, sometimes for minor things or even nothing. And don't forget those infamous rant videos featuring terms such as "[subject]? What, more like [mock name]! Oh my god, this [thing] sucks", "they like to go on failure adventures together", "Do you know who likes/hates this [thing]", "[subject] sucks, and so does [another subject]! [yet another subject] is [long number] times better than [subject]!", etc.

Basically, what used to be an easy-to-use animation tool ended up becoming Gen Z brainrot. In order to appeal to businesses (which contrary to popular belief, is NOT because of the grounded videos), the site became subscription-based and eventually changed its name in 2018 to the aforementioned Vyond, but by that point, the damage has already been done, and the site ended up creating one of the largest internet rabbit holes in history, full of kids who try hating preschool shows just to look "cool and mature" (or at least try to, since they're mostly the exact opposite), and videos that are so bad, they're good.



Basically, for those who are wondering, yes, the site did offer MIDI music in its early days, alongside some non-MIDI music.

Good for industrial levels, overworlds and cutscenes.

title: Gravity Circuit - Trippin' On The Electric Floor ⚡ ~ Theme Of Cable - Power Circuit (Remix)
description:
Did a special birthday arrangement of Theme Of Cable - Power Circuit from Gravity Circuit.

WARNING: The following contains a hoodie getting obsessive over an indie platformer. Viewer discretion advised.
This... is... AAAAAAAAAAAAA!!! WORDS CANNOT EXPRESS HOW AMAZING THIS SONG IS!!! Dominic Ninmark (most known for his works on Mega Man X: Corrupted and now Gravity Circuit) is a living legend of a composer, and I am one of his MANY simps. Dude makes some absolute bangers. Dude was literally the reason why I even tried the demo out in the first place (and fell in love with it).

I highly recommend Gravity Circuit. It is quite literally one of the best indie games that we were given. We, as a society, do not deserve this game... WE, AS A SOCIETY, DO NOT DESERVE THIS MASTERPIECE OF ART!!!


Important:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. E Minor (Original Pitch) [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. F Minor (Custom Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. Enables Voice Clip [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. Disables Voice Clip

name: smwmusic-hall-of-mirrors
title: Hall Of Mirrors
description:
Welcome to the null and void, where you and everything within will leave behind their own afterimages... oh wait, the SNES normally doesn't do this. Nevertheless, you may have noticed that some time ago I started using a game name of "Hall Of Mirrors Effect" for a few of my songs as part of an indirect series of songs. This is the titular song, and it also compliments the Strange Hub song via the same utilization of the Legend of Zelda: A Link To The Past's Mirror song sample (though the quality was increased somewhat), as well as some instrument samples straight out of the song for extra flavor.

Contains four user defines: one is a master echo enable switch, and a second one enables it for the music. Echo for SFX (though I tuned it so that the effect doesn't go too far into the seemingly endless), within the context of AddmusicK 1.0.10, the latest moderated version at the time of this release, (which still requires the master echo enable switch to be on) is handled through 1DFA commands $05 and $06: use 1DFA command $06 right after the song starts to enable echo for SFX. A third one enables all of the panning commands (without them, the song is in mono), and the last one enables a surround effect. The latter also requires panning to be enabled in order to be used.

name: smwmusic-haunted-castle-last-belmont-standing-don-t-wait-until-the-night-remix
title: Haunted Castle - Last Belmont Standing ~ Don't Wait Until The Night (Remix)
description:
𝕯𝖗𝖆𝖈𝖚𝖑𝖆. 𝕯𝖎𝖊 𝖓𝖔𝖜, 𝖆𝖓𝖉 𝖑𝖊𝖆𝖛𝖊 𝖙𝖍𝖎𝖘 𝖜𝖔𝖗𝖑𝖉! 𝖄𝖔𝖚'𝖑𝖑 𝖓𝖊𝖛𝖊𝖗 𝖇𝖊𝖑𝖔𝖓𝖌 𝖍𝖊𝖗𝖊!

A remix of the last stage theme in the Haunted Castle arcade game, Don't Wait Until The Night (which is also heard in the battle against Julius Belmont in Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow.

This song works best in castles, factories, towers, final areas, & other levels with intense vibes.

Note:
There is a ADD ME TO ADDMUSICK.txt file that has the sample bank that you need to move to Addmusic_sample_groups.txt. Thunder and Yoshi sound effects are disabled.
There are two customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song file:
- e minor (the default pitch specifically for this remix)
- d minor (The original pitch from the games)

versions.title: Haunted Castle - Last Belmont Standing ~ Don't Wait Until The Night (Remix)

name: smwmusic-haunted-castle-order-of-the-holy-spirit-cross-your-heart-remix
title: Haunted Castle - Order of the Holy Spirit ~ Cross Your Heart (Remix)
description:
𝖂𝖍𝖆𝖙 𝖆 𝖍𝖔𝖗𝖗𝖎𝖇𝖑𝖊 𝖓𝖎𝖌𝖍𝖙 𝖙𝖔 𝖍𝖆𝖛𝖊 𝖆 𝖈𝖚𝖗𝖘𝖊!

This is an arrangement Cross Your Heart, the first stage theme from Konami's Castlevania arcade game Haunted Castle. I had this song stuck in my head for about a week and decided to let it out of my head and into a port.

This song can fit castle, factories, towers, and intense levels / scenarios.

Note:
There is a !! Read Me!!.txt file that has the sample bank that you need to move to Addmusic_sample_groups.txt. Thunder and Yoshi sound effects are disabled.
There are three customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song file:
- f# minor (The default pitch from the original game)
- g minor (Based on Crucifix Held Close from Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin)
- e minor (A custom pitch that I thought sounded pretty cool for this song)

If you haven't already, check out Ultima's arrangement of Crucifix Held Close, a similar song from Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin. It's a well-crafted arrangement that some may prefer over this one if you liked that version better than what Haunted Castle had to offer.

mod note: the $EE command used in versions 1 and 2 detunes certain sound effects very slightly.

versions.title: Haunted Castle - Order of the Holy Spirit ~ Cross Your Heart (Remix)

name: smwmusic-hebereke-no-oishii-puzzle-wa-irimasen-ka-crossword
title: Hebereke no Oishii Puzzle wa Irimasen ka - Crossword
description:
Hebereke no Oishii Puzzle wa Irimasen ka, for those curious, is just the SNES version of the Sunsoft arcade game Oishii Puzzle wa Irimasen ka, but this time featuring characters from Sunsoft's Hebereke video game series. It's basically a party game consisting of you guessed it, puzzle mini games.

This song plays during the Crossword mini game, which NGL, is a HUGE language barrier, as obviously, that game was never released outside of Japan, and there isn't even a fan translation yet.

Note that this game uses Opus's "SQ & DBOOT" sound driver (undoubtedly the second most used sound driver on Super Famicom games, only behind Nintendo's Kankichi-kun/N-SPC sound driver; it was even used in the first-party game Mario's Super Picross), which is infamous for constantly shuffling channels during song playback, and because of that, porting songs from games using that sound driver would be a complete nightmare.

Therefore, I had to recreate the entire song from scratch, using the original instruments, samples, volumes, panning and echo, but without shuffling the channels this time, although fortunately, there aren't any notable inaccuracies in this port that I could find.

Good for puzzle levels, overworlds and cutscenes.

description:
A boss variation of the original song I made before this one, Groovin' Through The Streets. Leaned in more towards JRPG battle themes for this bad boy, especially with battle & boss themes from SNES Final Fantasy and Mega Man Battle Network.

Important:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," & Thunder SFX are disabled.
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ Death sound is gonna sound weird (@0 replaces @9 to save on space).

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. F Minor (Original Pitch) [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. E Minor (Custom Pitch 1)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. F# Minor (Custom Pitch 2)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ4. G Minor (Custom Pitch 3)

Also, there's an option to change compatibility to either support the Yoshi SFX or P-Switch Music:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. Enables Yoshi SFX, but Disables P-Switch Music [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. Enables P-Switch Music, but Disables Yoshi SFX

name: smwmusic-icrawfish-walls-that-are-still-called-home
title: icrawfish - Walls That Are Still Called Home
description:
My submission for 120hoSPC #12, a remix of icrawfish's Walls That Were Once Called Home, which won 3rd place.

The song tells of a familiar place, where many a memory continues to be made; though it'll one day be but a memory, it's still here and whole today, time not having made its mark yet. Tangible as these might be, these cozy walls are often taken for granted. I think we all have these kinds of places, and they might slip away as time goes on, so this remix serves as a celebration of those places, and a reminder to cherish those feelings and memories, right here right now!

name: smwmusic-ikachan-battle-inside-water
title: Ikachan - Battle Inside Water
description:
A really energectic, and upbeat remix of a calm, and happy song from Ikachan.
Man, this one was really challenging to remix, considering how this original theme's so peaceful, to make something really tense and upbeat. However, it was really worth the result it become in the end, am happy with what I've done.

Anyway, this remix's based on both the original Mizuno, AND this early version as well, found on the early OrgView files, named as "mizu[水の中で].mid", which was where I based off the string parts, this mix's pitch, and other small things, that I worked on.

name: smwmusic-ikachan-magirete
title: Ikachan - Magirete
description:
A cute song, used on the controls screen of Ikachan. It was apparently also a theme song for Pixel's dev room.

It does uses the KDL3 soundfont.

There's a plenty of define options for this song, where two of them fast forward, or slow downs the song (and pitch), and an option for make the percussions audible again (as the original puts them all the way down to volume 1, for some reason). If you want either of those options, open the text file, and change one of those define values, by anything other than 0.

Original description by Pixel
Original:
○雨に紛れて：開発室Pixelのテーマ曲だった。
Rough translation:
• Behind the rain: It was the theme song of the development room Pixel.

name: smwmusic-inside-the-machine
title: Inside the Machine
description:
Inside the Machine, a composition composed for Super Famicompo 4. It ranked 7th place in the 'Originals' category.

The zip file contains two .txts, an original submission including a define for turning off the intro, as well as a modified version that cuts down echo delay and vanilla samples to additionally minimize SFX channel usage, using two extra string samples.

If you're using the original submission, make sure to copy over the #InsideTheMachine sample group (only omits Thunder/Blaarg).

If you're using the modified version, copy over #InsideTheMachineModified sample group (omits @15/Yoshi, @7/Bonus End and Thunder/Blaarg).

name: smwmusic-iosys-super-world-cirno-s-perfect-math-class-remix
title: IOSYS - SUPER ⑨ WORLD ❄️ ~ Cirno's Perfect Math Class (Remix)
description:
𝗜'𝗹𝗹 𝗱𝗲𝗲𝗽-𝗳𝗿𝗲𝗲𝘇𝗲 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝘀𝗼𝗺𝗲 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵 𝗯𝗲𝗲𝗳!!



Did a special arrangement of IOSYS's Cirno's Perfect Math Class (which is a famous arrangement of Cirno's theme in Touhou 6, Beloved Tomboyish Girl) for a special event that's happening in September. It's . Another banger song to have arranged, and it's another remix based off another remix.

As someone who's not a fan of a majority of IOSYS's "meme" (I don't know how else to describe them) songs, I genuinely really like this one, especially given how much more upbeat this one is. Always been a fan of 2000s internet culture, and this is one of the reasons why.

Important:
♠ "Bonus End," Yoshi, P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. D Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. C Minor (Chill Penguin Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. Enables Voice Clip, but at the cost of SMW-Compatibility
2. Disables Voice Clip & Lowers Echo Buffer (turned on default)

versions.title: IOSYS - SUPER ⑨ WORLD ❄️ ~ Cirno's Perfect Math Class (Remix)

description:

name: smwmusic-jesus-dream-for-two-two-people-in-a-dream-remix
title: Jesus - Dream for Two ~ Two People In a Dream (Remix)
description:
My submission to 120hoSPC#10, which won 2nd place.

Per the rules of the contest, this song only uses one sample (@13). The tune itself is heavily remixed, with a sort of "1950's jazz" style to it. I would've liked to have captured more of the counter-melody that the original has going on, what with this being a song about two people and all, but I'm still content with how it came out.

I realized the song sounded good when I slowed it in the SPC player with pitch sync on, so I added a "Slowed & Reverb" toggle option.

(And no, the game has nothing to do with the Jesus you're thinking of, it's a spaceship :))

versions.title: Jesus - Dream for Two ~ Two People In a Dream (Remix)

name: smwmusic-jojo-s-bizarre-adventure-battle-tendency-divine-hamon-bloody-stream-remix
title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Battle Tendency - Divine Hamon ~ Bloody Stream (Remix)
description:
𝐍𝐢𝐠𝐞𝐫𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐨!!!

Did an arrangement of Bloody Stream from Jojo's Bizarre Adventure (Part 2): Battle Tendency. Had this on my mind for months ever since I did that Chase remix but never had the guts to do it until now. Sick opening theme and was my first favorite before hearing everything else and this... dropping from first to fifth (Chase, Crazy Noisy Bizarre Town, Sono Chi No Sadame, and Stand Proud beat it for me). Funny enough, it also reminds me way too much of Divine Bloodlines and Septette for the Dead Princess (should be no surprise to anyone who knows how much I love both songs).

Important:
♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There's also an option to enable or disable the loop in the song file with an ending like in the OP:
1. Loop (turned on by default)
2. No Loop (like in the original)

name: smwmusic-jojo-s-bizarre-adventure-diamond-is-unbreakable-chase-opening
title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Diamond is Unbreakable - Chase ~ Opening 2 (Remix)
description:
𝐕𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲 𝐢𝐬 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐛𝐲 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐭𝐲. 𝐓𝐡𝐚𝐭'𝐬 𝐰𝐡𝐲 𝐈'𝐥𝐥 𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐲𝐨𝐮.

Yes, I did a remix of Chase from Jojo's Bizarre Adventure (Part 4): Diamond is Unbreakable. You're not seeing things. It's my favorite of the Jojo OP themes and is by far one of the most underrated ones in the series. The hard rock combined with the deep emotion set piece really sets the mood for the entire song. Note, this isn't the actual full song and is just based on the OP version, since doing the full song would take up so much ARAM.

This baby can fit title screens, credits, [final] boss fights, intense stages, final areas, and castle / towers stages.

Important:
There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."
- "Bonus End" is disabled.

There's also an option to enable or disable the loop in the song file with an ending like in the OP:
1. Loops the song (turned on by default).
2. No Loop

name: smwmusic-jungle-village
title: Jungle Village
description:
Here's a potential jungle-esque level theme from my archives.

Welcome to the archival series! This was created for a conceptual SNES homebrew project (yes, a homebrew project, not a Super Mario World romhack) that I was going to create all the way back in 2007-2008 or so... well... until I lost most of the music in a hard drive crash, and subsequently the iteration is mostly lost except for a few songs that were created on the G3, of which this is one of them. These songs were never authentic SNES music in the first place, mostly because they pre-date SNESMod's entire existence and also pre-date my ability to compile the tools (XMSNES did exist, though, which was by the same author). And on your side, to my knowledge you really only had Addmusic Java to work with, to put in perspective how long ago this was. Therefore, until recently, these songs were never properly checked for sample filesize in particular and thus were never ported over. This one was initially done on 10/7/07.

WARNING: This song is not compatible with the speed-up effect of the Hurry Up! SFX. This is mostly because the main sample backing used here is tempo sensitive.

description:
❝ 𝐇𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐬𝐞𝐥𝐟 𝐚 𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐇𝐨𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐡𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐦𝐚𝐬! ❞

You all have been nice this Christmas, so you're getting a special arrangement of Frozen Hillside from Kirby Air Ride (ft. way too many songs). Been addicted to Kirby Air Riders for the past few weeks, and I thought it'd be sick to make my X-MAS SPECIAL SNES-MIX another Kirby Mashup. Thought it'd be neat to turn Frozen Hillside into a rock-inspired track heavily inspired by Ruined Castle Corridor & Silver Wolf (from Castlevania: Harmony of Despair & Mega Man Zero 2 respectively).

I never really liked this song growing up, but I've grown to appreciate it way more after playing Kirby Air Riders recently to where it's one of my favorite race track themes from the game.

Did a take on Yogurt Yard from Kirby's Adventure. Given how much I love the Kirby series, it is surprising that I went this far without doing any song from that franchise.

I love Yogurt Yard. It's definitely my favorite song in Kirby's Adventure and in my top 5 Kirby themes for sure. It's super catchy, upbeat, and "poppy" which is very fitting for the game it's in. Always preferred the cute side of Kirby more than the "dark 'n epic" side of him.

The first ever remix I ever uploaded (not SNES specifically) was a remix of Sand Canyon 2 from Dreamland 3 (it was bad, but a starting point at least), making this the second Kirby remix I made.

title: Kirby's Return To Dreamland - Border Of Life ~ Fly, Kirby! (Remix)
description:
Bravo, Kirby. You've truly earned your reputation as a hero.

Did an arrangement of Fly, Kirby! (Another Dimension) from Kirby's Return To Dreamland, one of my favorite games on the Wii (alongside Epic Yarn) and in the series. Wanted to do this for a while to celebrate Kirby's Return To Dreamland Deluxe, but I had a better idea to do it for an April Fools joke special instead. It's one of my favorite songs in the game and is easily the best shoot-em-up stage theme in the series (this is a hill I will die on).

Joke
Ninjitsu Art of Duplication!

Did an arrangement of Border Of Life from Touhou 7: Perfect Cherry Blossom. Ngl, not a big fan of the original song, so I thought I'd base this arrangement off the one in Kirby's Return to Dreamland. It's so cool ZUN gave Jun Ishikawa the rights to arrange the song 'cuz he made it even better than before!!!


Important:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," Yoshi, P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. F Minor (Custom Pitch 2)

description:
𝒪𝓊𝓇 𝑔𝓇𝓊𝒹𝑔𝑒 𝓌𝒾𝓁𝓁 𝒷𝑒 𝓈𝑒𝓉𝓉𝓁𝑒𝒹 𝒶𝓉 𝓁𝒶𝓈𝓉...
𝑀𝑒𝑒𝓉 𝓂𝓎 𝓅𝑜𝓌𝑒𝓇𝒻𝓊𝓁 𝓈𝑒𝒸𝓇𝑒𝓉 𝓌𝑒𝒶𝓅𝑜𝓃...
𝒯𝒽𝑒 𝒷𝓇𝒶𝓃𝒹-𝓃𝑒𝓌 𝒟𝑒𝒹𝑒𝒹𝑒 𝐻𝒶𝓂𝓂𝑒𝓇!

Did an arrangement of the one and only, Masked Dedede's Theme, from Kirby Super Star Ultra for my 5K subscriber milestone. A massive goal reached deserves some treatment from the King himself. I already did his theme once... now it's time to do it again!!!

It shouldn't be a surprise when I say this is my favorite Kirby theme and one of my favorite final boss themes in any video game period. Seriously, to top the original song (which is already one of the best songs in the series) with this is an achievement very few can achieve.

Important:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ Death sound is gonna sound weird (@1 replaces @9 to save on space).

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. C# Minor w/ slight detune (Remix Pitch - Listening Only)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. C# Minor (Remix Pitch) [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. C Minor (Original Pitch)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ4. B Minor (GaMetal Pitch)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ5. D Minor (Candid Friend Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. Enables Voice Clips, but at the cost of SMW-Compatibility
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. Disables Voice Clips [turned on default]

versions.title: Kirby Super Star Ultra - Vengeance, The Mask's Awakening ~ Masked Dedede (Remix)

description:
A nice water-y or ruins song with some big stakes involved.

I don't exactly know what its role was in-game since I discovered it browsing Zophar domain. So far it is the nicest track I could find in the whole OST, I hope you'll enjoy it as much as I do.

-------------
Important update:

On the former version, it was brought to my attention by Stivi, that calling Pause was not interrupting the song, but rather letting it freeze in place on the last played note.

It occurs on AddMusicK1.0.8 when channel #6, which plays the pause SFX, has noise inside, as explained by KungFuFurby and Kevin.

While I could have chosen to take #6's contents to channel #7, I found this choice inesthetical since #7 always gets cut with Jump or coin sounds. So I just replaced the noise sample of #6 by an external closed hat sample.

name: smwmusic-krack-the-hack-deeper-into-sins
title: Krack The Hack - Deeper Into Sins
description:
The second song from the bonus final level from Krack The Hack, originally an IDOL 8 entry that barely made it to the next round (the song was known as "Cyberspace Sanctuary" at the time). Made for high-tech space levels. There are a few differences between this version, the IDOL 8 version, and the version in Krack The Hack itself as a result of optimizing the port for a public release.

A "no staccato" define option is present for those who wants to save space. With staccato set to 1, it'll decrease the size to 0x0576 but will sound slightly worse (but accurate to how it was heard in Krack The Hack).

Samples from that IDOL 8 round was provided by Skewer.

name: smwmusic-krack-the-hack-sokobansolvermanianicazen-sins
title: Krack The Hack - Sokobansolvermanianicazen Sins
description:
The long repetitious bonus final level theme from Krack The Hack with a very long name to boot, originally made for Mario Must Die 3 until Sokobansolver decided to use a different theme instead. Made to be exciting training music made to fit multiple environments. There are a few differences between this version and the version in Krack The Hack itself as a result of optimizing the port for a public release.

A "no staccato" define option is present for those who wants to save space. With staccato set to 1, it'll decrease the size to 0x03A8 but will sound slightly worse (but accurate to how it was heard in Krack The Hack).

Taking a page off of Hooded Edge, there are two versions: an E Minor version (Krack pitch), and a D minor version (Daizo pitch). Pick either or to match your level as you wish!

This song isn't compatible with every SMW sample, but you're free to enable/disable what you need using the provided defines. By default I enabled LevelClear, Star, Death, and GameOver; which leaves out Thunder, Blargg, P-switch, Star, Bonus End, and Yoshi.

title: Labyrinth Forest of the Archmuse - Labyrinth Forest
description:
A dense and ever-looping tune, symbolizing the vast expanse of the Labyrinth Forest. Just when you've found a new corner to lead you closer to the truth, you find yourself right back where you began.

OPTION:
This song has an echo toggle option that controls how compatible with SMW the song is.
ECHO 1: uses #optimized, but minimal echo.
ECHO 5: More echo, but not compatible with Yoshi, Bonus End, P-switch, and Thunder (Miss uses @1).
ECHO 7: Listen-only, most faithful to source.

This was part of a larger song I made for a Battle of the Bits contest, where we were tasked with making a 5 minute long song in 4 hours. The intro and outro of that song have become this submission.

To see the other part, go here.
To see the original composition in full, go here.

description:
A solemn hymn, greeting travelers with a question as they enter the Labyrinth Forest, and likewise ushering them out with a similar tune as the travelers leave with the truth of the forest in tow. Good for cutscenes and more ethereal overworlds.

OPTIONS:
This song has 2 separate toggle options that control the key and version specifically. The first option has 3 settings for whether the song loops, ends early, or resolves, and the second option has 2 settings, to set either the key signature for the intro version or the outro version.

name: smwmusic-last-bible-iii-central-of-the-world-underworld-forest-remix
title: Last Bible III - Central of the World ~ Underworld Forest (Remix)
description:
Decided to make my 200th port upload on this site something special similar to my Air Man Remix in February, so I did a special remix of SMWC's National Anthem Underworld Forest from Last Bible III.

History Of The SMWC National Anthem
Six years ago, legendary porter Nanako made a port of this song, and little did anyone know that it'd change the entire Super Mario World industry. Nearly every SMW hack had this theme in it in some way or form. You could not escape it, even if you tried. And to make things worse, a year ago, other legendary porter Samantha made an unsampled port to add to the chaos. SMWCentral has never been the same since. What was once an innocent web site for gamers who wanted to express their love for the amazing Super Mario World has now turned into an Underworld Forest cult. SMWCentral deprived themselves of their Super Mario World content in order to please the Underworld Forest god with using this song in their hacks. This site is stuck in an endless cycle of torture of making sure this song was engraved into our brains, note for note, and us porters are forced to port / arrange this song or else our end will come. This is not just an end of an era. but it's the true end of... The Time-when-Underworld-Forest-wasn't-a-thing Days...


Jokes aside though, this song's absolutely fantastic (and so are those ports). There's a reason why so many people love using it, and I hope I was able to spice things up with my take on this awesome theme for my special! :D

Important:
♠ "Bonus End," & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. B Minor w/ slight detune (Remix Pitch, Listening-Only)
2. B Minor (Remix Pitch, turned on default)
2. C Minor (Original Pitch)
2. A# Minor (Custom Pitch)

versions.title: Last Bible III - Central of the World ~ Underworld Forest (Remix)

name: smwmusic-link-the-faces-of-evil-do-the-duck-walk-firestone-lake-remix
title: Link: The Faces Of Evil - DO THE DUCK WALK!! ~ Firestone Lake (Remix)
description:
❝ 𝑀𝒶𝒽 𝒷𝑜𝒾, 𝓉𝒽𝒾𝓈 𝓅𝑒𝒶𝒸𝑒 𝒾𝓈 𝓌𝒽𝒶𝓉 𝒶𝓁𝓁 𝓉𝓇𝓊𝑒 𝓌𝒶𝓇𝓇𝒾𝑜𝓇𝓈 𝓈𝓉𝓇𝒾𝓋𝑒 𝐹𝒪𝑅! ❞
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ- King Harkinian, 1993

Yes, you're not seeing things. I just did an actual SNES arrangement of Firestone Lake from Link: The Faces of Evil. I dunno if y'all know about this... but I'm UNIRONICALLY in love with the first two Zelda CD-I OSTs. I'm not kidding when I say this is some of my favorite Zelda music ever. Look, other old-school Zelda OSTs are good too, but William Havlicek just said "fuggit!" and gave us high-energy music. This doesn't sound like Zelda in the slightest, but who cares! I like it, and you will too!!!

Also, this is my first Zelda arrangement / port, and it had to be from this game, lmao.

Important:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. C / F Minor (Original Pitch) [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. C# / F# Minor (Ricky Martin Pitch)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. A / D Minor (Shrek 2 Pitch)

name: smwmusic-long-range-motivation
title: Long Range Motivation
description:
An original song I made in a competition of ORG Maker. I felt so happy with what I had composed, that I wanted to port it.
I think it doesn't seem to fit very well in a SMW level, unless someone use it wisely.

03/19/2021 Update
* Did rework the entire port from zero, so now every section is properly optimized, and the text file is MUCH MORE readable;
* Added more channels to fill the strings part, so it sounds much more fuller;
* Replaced the cymbal sample to the KSS one;
* Reworked on most of non Kirby samples, downgrading some, and making the organ-like wave more higher quality;
* Crammed all of the percussion parts in one single channel;
* Added a second text file which does contain the final section of the song (which is where the actual song ends, instead of looping forever). Keep in mind that the full one loops once, then it'll stay silent, like the original piece;
* Lowered the global volume to w166.


03/22/2021 Update: Just a small fix on the organ-like wave sample on the full version, where the highest note channel overflows at the final section.

name: smwmusic-lost-desert
title: Lost Desert
description:
I originally made this song for a 100% free (with no in-game-real-money payments) sidescroller MMORPG game called Aeon Rivals back in 2017 when it was in development.

It was originally for the Lost Desert level, as the author was requesting for .XM music to be put into the game.

I gave the author this song and while he liked it, he couldn't put it in the game because I was 14 at the time, so I was too young to be able to receive payment without complications.

Of course, I'm still too young now, and it seems the game is already done, so I'll just upload the song here. Well, converted to AddMusicK MML.

This might not sound like most other desert themes. I tried to go not for the classic Saharan feel, but for a more southern US atmosphere that is also mysterious.

And yes, I lifted the drum samples from Evanescence's Bring Me To Life stems.

description:
𝐃𝐞𝐬-𝐩𝐚-𝐜𝐢𝐭𝐨
𝐐𝐮𝐢𝐞𝐫𝐨 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐫 𝐭𝐮 𝐜𝐮𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐨 𝐝𝐞𝐬𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐭𝐨
𝐃𝐞𝐣𝐚 𝐪𝐮𝐞 𝐭𝐞 𝐝𝐢𝐠𝐚 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐚𝐬 𝐚𝐥 𝐨í𝐝𝐨
𝐏𝐚𝐫𝐚 𝐪𝐮𝐞 𝐭𝐞 𝐚𝐜𝐮𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐬 𝐬𝐢 𝐧𝐨 𝐞𝐬𝐭á𝐬 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐦𝐢𝐠𝐨
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ- Luis Fonzi, 2017

No, you didn't just accidentally skip back to a 2017 meme compilation, this is a 2023 SNES remix of Despacito by Luis Fonsi (ft. Daddy Yankee). Let it be known that I don't understand 90% of the lyrics (despite knowing like 5% Spanish), but Despacito's got an amazing beat, and that's all that really matters.

Important:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End" Yoshi, & Thunder SFX are disabled.
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ Death sound is gonna sound weird (@0 replaces @9 to save on space).

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. B Minor w/ slight detune (Remix Pitch - Listening-Only)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. B Minor (Original Pitch) [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. A Minor (Custom Pitch 1)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ4. C Minor (Custom Pitch 2)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. Enables Nylon Intro & Voice Clip, but at the cost of SMW-Compatibility
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. Enables Nylon Intro Only, but at the cost of @12 [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. Disables Nylon Intro & Voice Clip

versions.title: Luiz Fonsi - Can't Handle The Rush! ~ Despacito (Remix)

name: smwmusic-machinations-m-t-opolitaines
title: Machinations Météopolitaines
description:
"You're walking through the big city, lost in thought. But, looking around, things aren't quite so bad when you're here."

A joint composition between icrawfish and bebn legg that won 4th place at Super Famicompo 4. We took turns composing and porting each part, which was lots of fun, and this fusion of a piece was the result.

We came up with the title by combining some themes the song reminded us, like cities and machines, but also seasonal/weathery vibes, and brought that over to French to come up with "Machinations Météopolitaines" (the second word being a combination of "météo" meaning weather, and "métropolitain", or metropolitan).

title: Mario is Missing! (NES) Expanded - Berlin Germany
description:
Ever wondered what the music would sound like if Mario is Missing! for the NES was ever expanded upon?
Well, I certainly was and the result was this!

It's a pretty neato composition I'd say, it captures some stuff from the original and turns it into something new.
The percussion is a bit of unhinged compered to how it is in the actual game, but I think it has a certain charm to it that compliments the song well.

Will I end up doing more?
Certainly, but not actively, maybe once a couple months.

Anyway, this song can be used in retro levels and cities.
It can be a bit repetitive after a while, so keep that in mind!
